title: ORMs and raw SQL: where injection survives
summary: EF Core and Dapper parameterize for you, until someone reaches for FromSqlRaw, ExecuteSqlRaw or a sort column from the query string. Learn which calls are safe, and allow-list what parameters cannot carry.

steps.title: LINQ is safe. Raw SQL is up to you.
body: ```csharp fragment
db.Products.Where(p => p.Name.Contains(q))                         // LINQ: always a parameter
db.Products.FromSql($"SELECT * FROM Products WHERE Name = {q}")     // safe: {q} becomes a parameter
db.Database.ExecuteSql($"UPDATE Products SET Hidden = 1 WHERE Id = {id}")   // safe
db.Database.SqlQuery<int>($"SELECT Id FROM Products WHERE Name = {q}")     // safe
db.Products.FromSqlRaw("SELECT * FROM Products WHERE Name = '" + q + "'")  // INJECTABLE
db.Products.FromSqlRaw($"SELECT * FROM Products WHERE Name = '{q}'")       // INJECTABLE: the trap
db.Products.FromSqlRaw("SELECT * FROM Products WHERE Name = {0}", q)       // safe: {0} is a parameter

The trap is the line with `$` and `FromSqlRaw`. It *looks* like the safe `FromSql` call, but `FromSqlRaw` takes a finished string, so C# fills in `q` before EF Core ever sees it. EF Core's analyzer warns about it (**EF1002**, "risk of vulnerability to SQL injection"): treat that warning as an error.
Dapper is the same story: `conn.Query<Product>("SELECT * FROM Products WHERE Name = @name", new { name = q })` is a parameter; `"... = '" + q + "'"` is not.

steps.explain: The last one is not injectable, but it does not work either: a parameter is a **value**, so `ORDER BY @p0` sorts by a constant string. Column names need an allow-list.

steps.title: What a parameter cannot carry
body: Parameters hold values. These parts of a query are **identifiers and keywords**, and must never come from the request as text:
- column and table names: `ORDER BY {sort}`, `SELECT {fields}`, a tenant's table name;
- sort direction: `ASC` / `DESC`;
- `LIMIT`/`TOP` built as text (use a parameter or LINQ's `Take`, and cap it).
Map the request's word to code you wrote, and refuse anything else:
```csharp fragment
query = sort switch
"name"   => query.OrderBy(p => p.Name),
"price"  => query.OrderBy(p => p.PriceCents),
"-price" => query.OrderByDescending(p => p.PriceCents),
_        => throw new ArgumentException("Unknown sort.")   // -> 400

And **LIKE**: a parameter stops injection, but `%` and `_` in the value are still wildcards. That is harmless for a search box; for an exact-prefix check (`WHERE Email LIKE @domain`), escape them or use `=`/`StartsWith`.

steps.prompt: The build shows `warning EF1002: Method 'FromSqlRaw' inserts interpolated strings directly into the SQL`. What is the right change?
options: Switch to `FromSql($"...")` (or LINQ), so the interpolated values become parameters
Suppress the warning: the values come from our own front-end
Escape the quotes in the values before interpolating
Move the query into a stored procedure that concatenates the same way
steps.explain: `FromSql` and `FromSqlInterpolated` turn each `{value}` into a `DbParameter`. Keep EF1002 as an error in CI (`<WarningsAsErrors>EF1002</WarningsAsErrors>`) so this never ships again.

steps.title: NoSQL injects too
body: Document databases have no SQL, but they have **operators**, and a JSON body can carry them:
```text
POST /login
{"username": "admin", "password": {"$ne": null}}

If that body is turned into a MongoDB filter as it is, the query becomes *username is admin and password is not null*: signed in without a password. The fix is the same idea as for SQL: bind the body to a typed record (`record Login(string Username, string Password)`), so an object where a string belongs fails to bind, and build filters with the driver's builders (`Builders<User>.Filter.Eq(u => u.Username, login.Username)`), never from raw JSON.

steps.title: Fix the EF Core search and its sort
prompt: Fix `List<string> Search(ShopDb db, string q, string sort)`. It returns product names that contain `q`, ordered by `sort`:
- `q` must be a **parameter** (`FromSql` with interpolation, or LINQ);
- `sort` is one of `name`, `price` (cheapest first), `-price` (dearest first); ties sort by name; anything else throws `ArgumentException`.
starter: List<string> Search(ShopDb db, string q, string sort) =>
.FromSqlRaw("SELECT * FROM Products WHERE Name LIKE '%" + q + "%' ORDER BY " + sort)
solution: List<string> Search(ShopDb db, string q, string sort)
var query = db.Products.FromSql($"SELECT * FROM Products WHERE Name LIKE {pattern}");
hints: Build the pattern first, then `db.Products.FromSql($"SELECT * FROM Products WHERE Name LIKE {pattern}")`. EF Core makes `{pattern}` a parameter.
Sorting: `query = sort switch { "name" => query.OrderBy(p => p.Name), ..., _ => throw new ArgumentException("Unknown sort.") };` EF Core wraps the raw SQL in a subquery and sorts outside it.
template: using var dojoConn = new SqliteConnection("Data Source=:memory:");
new Product { Name = "Night Owl O'Clock Lamp", PriceCents = 3900 },
Dojo.Try("sort by name", () => Dojo.Eq("lamp, by name", new List<string> { "Desk lamp", "Floor lamp", "Night Owl O'Clock Lamp" }, Search(dojoDb, "lamp", "name")));
Dojo.Try("sort by price", () => Dojo.Eq("lamp, cheapest first", new List<string> { "Night Owl O'Clock Lamp", "Desk lamp", "Floor lamp" }, Search(dojoDb, "lamp", "price")));
Dojo.Try("sort by price, descending", () => Dojo.Eq("lamp, dearest first", new List<string> { "Floor lamp", "Desk lamp", "Night Owl O'Clock Lamp" }, Search(dojoDb, "lamp", "-price")));
Dojo.Try("a quote in the search", () => Dojo.Eq("O'Clock is found", new List<string> { "Night Owl O'Clock Lamp" }, Search(dojoDb, "O'Clock", "name")));
Dojo.Try("a UNION payload", () => Dojo.Eq("' UNION SELECT ... finds nothing", new List<string>(), Search(dojoDb, "' UNION SELECT 99, 'pwned', 0--", "name")));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("a sort with SQL in it is refused", () => Search(dojoDb, "lamp", "PriceCents; DROP TABLE Products"));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("an unknown column is refused", () => Search(dojoDb, "lamp", "Id"));
Dojo.Eq("the products table is intact", 4, dojoDb.Products.Count());
